# Claude Code Multi-Agent Harness: What Actually Works in Production

## Executive Summary

The official Claude Code documentation is authoritative and detailed. Most of the architecture used in the Gidape harness is sound and aligns with official patterns — but several specific claims in CLAUDE.md and common community practice diverge from how the system actually works. This report distinguishes **official Anthropic documentation** (from `code.claude.com/docs`), **Anthropic engineering posts** (from `anthropic.com/engineering`), and **community practice** at every claim.

---

## 1. Native `.claude/agents/` Subagent Files

**Status: Fully documented and supported — official Anthropic docs.**

Source: [Create custom subagents — code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)

### How it works

- Subagent definitions are **Markdown files with YAML frontmatter** stored in `.claude/agents/` (project scope) or `~/.claude/agents/` (user scope).
- Each file has two required fields: `name` and `description`. Everything else is optional.
- The `description` is what Claude uses to decide **when to automatically delegate**. The better the description, the more reliably Claude routes to that subagent.
- Each subagent runs in **its own context window** with a custom system prompt — not the full Claude Code system prompt.
- Subagents inherit CLAUDE.md files from the main session (exception: built-in `Explore` and `Plan` subagents skip CLAUDE.md for speed).

### Complete supported frontmatter fields (official)

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | Lowercase + hyphens; this is what `agent_type` resolves to in hooks |
| `description` | Yes | What Claude reads to decide when to delegate |
| `tools` | No | Allowlist; inherits all tools if omitted |
| `disallowedTools` | No | Denylist applied before `tools` allowlist |
| `model` | No | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, full model ID (e.g. `claude-opus-4-8`), or `inherit` (default) |
| `permissionMode` | No | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan` |
| `maxTurns` | No | Hard cap on agentic turns |
| `skills` | No | Skills preloaded into context at startup |
| `mcpServers` | No | MCP servers scoped to this subagent only |
| `hooks` | No | Lifecycle hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) |
| `memory` | No | `user`, `project`, or `local` for cross-session persistent memory |
| `background` | No | `true` = always run as background task |
| `effort` | No | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `isolation` | No | `worktree` = isolated git worktree for this subagent |
| `color` | No | Display color in task list |
| `initialPrompt` | No | Auto-submitted first user turn when agent runs as main session via `--agent` |

### Critical constraint: subagents cannot spawn other subagents

> "Subagents cannot spawn other subagents. If your workflow requires nested delegation, use Skills or chain subagents from the main conversation." — official docs

This is a hard architectural limit. The `Agent` tool is **not available inside subagent context**. Any harness design that relies on subagents spawning further subagents will silently fail.

### `subagent_type` parameter

The term `subagent_type` appears in hooks context, not as an invocation parameter. Specifically: `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` hooks receive the agent's `name` field value as the `agent_type` matcher input. When using `--agents` CLI JSON, you reference agents by key name. When using `Agent(agent_type)` syntax in tools allowlist, the parenthesized value is the agent's `name`.

**Note on tool rename:** As of Claude Code v2.1.63, the `Task` tool was renamed to `Agent`. `Task(...)` references in existing configurations still work as aliases.

---

## 2. Slash Commands (`.claude/commands/`)

**Status: Supported but officially deprecated in favor of `.claude/skills/`. Both work.**

Source: [Slash Commands in the SDK — code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/slash-commands](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/slash-commands), [Best practices — code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

### What they are

- Markdown files in `.claude/commands/` (project) or `~/.claude/commands/` (user).
- The filename (without `.md`) becomes the slash command: `review.md` → `/review`.
- Optional YAML frontmatter supports: `description`, `allowed-tools`, `model`, `argument-hint`.
- `$ARGUMENTS` (or `$0`, `$1` etc.) inserts user arguments.
- Commands can embed `!`\`bash command\`` to run live shell output at invocation time.
- Can reference file contents with `@path/to/file`.

### Do slash commands trigger multi-agent pipelines?

**No directly, but yes indirectly.** A slash command is a prompt template — it runs in the main conversation context. It can instruct Claude to "use the security-reviewer subagent to…" and Claude will then invoke the Agent tool to spawn the subagent. The command itself does not mechanically spawn agents; it issues instructions that Claude then executes, including delegating to subagents.

The recommended modern replacement is `.claude/skills/` with `SKILL.md` files. Skills support the same `/name` invocation plus **autonomous invocation** (Claude can load them without being explicitly told to). The CLI continues to support both formats.

---

## 3. CLAUDE.md: Documented Limitations and Recommended Size

**Status: Officially documented with explicit warnings about length.**

Source: [Best practices — code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

### The official guidance (verbatim)

> "Keep it concise. For each line, ask: 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?' If not, cut it. **Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!**"

> "CLAUDE.md is loaded every session, so only include things that apply broadly."

> Recommended: **under 200 lines, under 2,000 tokens.**

> "The most important resource to manage [is] Claude's context window. LLM performance degrades as context fills."

### What causes CLAUDE.md instructions to be ignored

The best-practices docs explicitly call out the failure mode: a CLAUDE.md that is too long causes important rules to get lost in noise. The failure pattern is named: **"The over-specified CLAUDE.md"** — if Claude keeps violating a rule, the fix is to ruthlessly prune the file, not add more.

### CLAUDE.md can import other files

Via `@path/to/file` syntax — this is the correct pattern for large contextual documents. Reference them from a concise CLAUDE.md rather than inlining everything.

### What CLAUDE.md does NOT do

- It is **advisory**, not deterministic. Rules can be missed.
- For deterministic enforcement, use **hooks** (scripts that run at lifecycle events, cannot be ignored).
- CLAUDE.md files are loaded into every subagent's context too (except built-in Explore and Plan).

### Implication for the Gidape harness

The current `CLAUDE.md` is far over the recommended 200-line / 2,000-token threshold. This is a documented cause of instruction-following degradation. The `@path/to/import` mechanism should be used to split content into imported files, keeping the root CLAUDE.md under the threshold.

---

## 4. Orchestrator Pattern: Claude Code Sessions vs. API

**Status: The orchestrator-calls-subagents pattern is natively supported in Claude Code sessions via the Agent tool.**

Sources: [code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents), [code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams), [anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)

### Two separate systems

**System A — Subagents (within a single session):**
- One Claude instance (the main conversation) uses the **Agent tool** to spawn subagents.
- Each subagent has its own context window and returns only a summary to the main context.
- Subagents are defined in `.claude/agents/` files OR created ad-hoc by Claude.
- Subagents **cannot spawn further subagents** — depth is fixed at 1.
- This is stable and available in all Claude Code versions.

**System B — Agent Teams (multiple coordinated sessions, experimental):**
- Requires `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` in settings.
- Requires Claude Code v2.1.32+.
- A team lead creates teammates — separate Claude Code instances — with a shared task list and mailbox.
- Teammates can communicate directly with each other, not just back to the lead.
- Teammates **cannot spawn their own teams** (no nesting).
- Marked explicitly as experimental with known limitations: no session resumption with in-process teammates, task status can lag, one team at a time.

### Anthropic's Multi-Agent Research System

Source: [anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)

This is Anthropic's internal research tool. Key verified facts:
- Uses **Claude Opus 4** as lead agent, **Claude Sonnet 4** as subagents. This mix outperformed single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2%.
- The document does **not specify** whether it runs on the Messages API directly or via Claude Code sessions — the implementation details are not disclosed.
- The pattern described (lead agent decomposes task → spawns parallel specialist subagents → synthesizes) is the same pattern that `.claude/agents/` + the Agent tool implements in Claude Code.
- Key production lessons: error handling with checkpoints, observability without reading contents, rainbow deployments, external memory for long research, routing subagent output to filesystem instead of funneling through lead context.

**Conclusion:** The orchestrator pattern applies to both API-level multi-agent systems and Claude Code sessions. The Claude Code Agent tool is the mechanism for Claude Code sessions.

---

## 5. Subagents vs. Agent Teams: The Practical Difference

**Status: Officially documented with a comparison table.**

Source: [code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams)

| | Subagents | Agent Teams |
|---|---|---|
| Context | Own context; results return to main | Own context; fully independent |
| Communication | Report results to main agent only | Teammates message each other directly |
| Coordination | Main agent manages all work | Shared task list + self-coordination |
| Best for | Focused tasks where only result matters | Complex work requiring discussion |
| Token cost | Lower (results summarized back) | Higher (each is a separate Claude instance) |
| Stability | Stable | Experimental, with known limitations |
| Subagent nesting | No | No (teammates cannot spawn teams) |

**The critical difference:** subagents in `.claude/agents/` can be referenced by agent teams when spawning teammates, giving you the ability to define a role once and use it in both patterns.

---

## 6. Slash Commands vs. Skills: The Current State

**Status: Skills (`.claude/skills/`) are the current recommended format; commands (`.claude/commands/`) are legacy but still supported.**

Source: [code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

Skills (`SKILL.md` files) support:
- Same `/name` slash invocation as commands
- **Autonomous invocation** — Claude can load and apply them without being explicitly told, based on relevance
- `disable-model-invocation: true` for workflows that should only run when explicitly triggered
- Can specify `context: fork` to run skill in a forked subagent

Slash commands (`.claude/commands/`) are listed as legacy. The CLI supports both. There is no migration urgency, but new harnesses should use Skills.

---

## 7. Is CLAUDE.md Orchestration Architecturally Correct?

**Status: Partially correct by design, but structurally limited.**

### What works

Using CLAUDE.md to define orchestration behavior (which subagents to invoke, when, in what sequence) is a **supported pattern** according to official docs. CLAUDE.md is read by the main session and by subagents (except Explore/Plan). Orchestration instructions in CLAUDE.md are advisory — Claude reads them and acts on them via the Agent tool.

### What does NOT work (hard constraints)

1. **Subagents spawning subagents**: impossible. If your CLAUDE.md instructs a subagent to "call harness-evaluator after harness-builder finishes," the subagent cannot do this — the Agent tool is unavailable inside subagent context. Only the main session can spawn subagents.

2. **CLAUDE.md length causing instruction loss**: at the documented threshold (~2,000 tokens), instructions become unreliable. A complex pipeline defined entirely in CLAUDE.md will experience degraded adherence.

3. **CLAUDE.md is not deterministic**: instructions can be missed or deprioritized. For guaranteed execution (lint before commit, security check on migration files), use hooks in `.claude/settings.json`.

### What is the correct architecture

The correct multi-layer approach is:

- **CLAUDE.md** (concise, <2000 tokens): project conventions, naming, absolute rules. Use `@path/to/file` imports for detailed docs.
- **`.claude/agents/`**: define specialized subagents with precise descriptions so Claude knows when to delegate automatically or on request.
- **`.claude/settings.json` hooks**: for deterministic lifecycle enforcement (SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop).
- **Skills** (`.claude/skills/`): reusable prompts/workflows invokable as slash commands or autonomously.
- **CLAUDE.md orchestration routing**: acceptable for soft routing guidance, not for hard pipeline enforcement.

---

Anthropic uses the term "harness" to mean "the orchestration framework that coordinates agent execution." The key concept is **dynamic workflows** — Claude Opus 4.8+ can write its own orchestration harness (JavaScript) on the fly for each task rather than always using the static default. This is distinct from static CLAUDE.md-based orchestration. Dynamic workflows can: decide which models subagents use, run subagents in isolated worktrees, resume from checkpoints, process data programmatically.

## 9. Adversarial Verification: Claims That Need Correction

### Claim: "harness-builder invokes harness-evaluator"

**Partially incorrect.** If harness-builder runs as a subagent, it cannot spawn harness-evaluator (or any subagent). The main orchestrator session must invoke evaluator after builder returns. The pipeline in CLAUDE.md should direct the **orchestrator** to call both in sequence, not builder to call evaluator.

### Claim: Agent tool with `subagent_type` parameter

**Needs precision.** The `subagent_type` term appears in hooks documentation (as the value passed to `agent_type` matchers in SubagentStart/Stop hooks). When Claude invokes the Agent tool, it identifies the target subagent by its `name` field. The `--agents` CLI flag accepts a JSON object where keys are agent names. There is no separate "subagent_type" invocation parameter in the Agent tool itself — the routing is by name.

### Claim: `.claude/agents/` supports specifying provider (Claude vs. Gemini)

**Not supported via frontmatter.** The `model` field accepts model aliases and full Anthropic model IDs only (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, or `claude-*` IDs). Non-Anthropic models are not selectable via the `model` frontmatter field. Running Gemini models as subagents requires an MCP server or external tool bridge, not native frontmatter routing.

### Claim: CLAUDE.md orchestration is reliable for multi-step pipelines

**Conditionally true.** Works for soft routing if the file is concise. Fails for hard enforcement if the file is bloated. The official docs are explicit: long CLAUDE.md = ignored instructions. For a pipeline as complex as the Gidape harness, the instructions will compete with each other for attention.

## 10. Recommended Architecture for the Gidape Harness (Synthesis)

Based entirely on official documentation:

1. **Slim CLAUDE.md to <200 lines.** Use `@.harness/constitution.md`, `@.harness/memory-bank/product.md` etc. via import syntax. The routing table and pipeline description belong in imported files.

2. **`.claude/agents/` files for every subagent.** Currently working correctly. Descriptions are the routing mechanism — make them precise and include "use proactively when..." phrasing.

3. **Main session as orchestrator.** The orchestrator cannot be a subagent. The main Claude Code session invokes Agent tool → routes to subagents → receives summaries → chains to next agent. This matches the current design.

4. **Use hooks for deterministic gates.** Instead of CLAUDE.md instructions like "always run security-reviewer on auth files," configure a `SubagentStart` or `PostToolUse` hook in `.claude/settings.json` that fires based on file pattern.

5. **Agent Teams for true parallelism.** When builder and evaluator need to run concurrently and communicate, Agent Teams (experimental) is the correct feature. Today's sequential delegation (builder → evaluator) is correct for the non-experimental path.

6. **Subagent cannot call subagent.** Any spec that describes "harness-builder spawns harness-evaluator" must be revised: the orchestrator must chain them.
